translationRepairs: In Song times He Chengtian further took 26/49 as the strong rate and 9/17 as the weak rate, seeking the day divisor at the juncture of strong and weak.
In the Liu Song, He Chengtian further took 26/49 as the strong rate and 9/17 as the weak rate, seeking the day divisor at the juncture of strong and weak.
Chinese 宋世 here means the Liu Song dynasty (何承天), not the Northern Song of this treatise; the idiomatic field already says Liu Song.
Historians ought to gather the motions of sun and moon to seek conjunction at new moon.
Astronomical officials ought to gather the motions of sun and moon to seek conjunction at new moon.
史官 in this calendrical treatise means court astronomical officials, matching the idiomatic "Astronomers"; "Historians" is misleading.
The calendar was then named the Mingtian Calendar. Hanlin Academician Wang Gui was ordered to write a preface, and Cong also composed an explanatory summary to stand at the beginning.
It was then granted the name Mingtian Calendar; an edict directed Hanlin Academician Wang Gui to write a preface, and Cong also composed an explanatory summary to head it.
Chinese has 詔 before 翰林學士王珪序之; the idiomatic version drops the edict governing Wang Gui's preface order that the literal preserves.
